Hi Anna — thanks for the clear question. Below is a short, sharable explanation you can drop into legal + procurement, followed by the pilot concession we can include in the SOW.

Short explanation for procurement/legal:
- Aggregation: Redwood aggregates token usage across all API calls for the billing month and compares the aggregated total to the contracted monthly minimum. That means we do not apply the minimum on a per-call basis.
- Rounding & billing quantum: We bill in 100-token units. Aggregated monthly usage is rounded up to the nearest 100 tokens before the floor is applied. This reduces overcharging risk from many tiny calls.

Pilot concession (proposed SOW clause):
- 3-month smoothing credit: For the initial three billing cycles after SOW execution Redwood will apply a smoothing credit equal to the difference between the contracted monthly minimum and Brightcart’s aggregated usage for that month, capped at 25% of the contracted minimum in any month. Smooth credits are applied as token credits on invoices and are reconciled at the end of the third month. If Brightcart’s usage exceeds the contracted minimum in months 2–3, smoothing credits will be reduced pro rata.
- Conditions: requires a signed SOW, a brief anonymized usage histogram (call counts by token-bucket ranges) shared weekly for the pilot period, and is limited to this pilot only.
